decisions.decision: M4.6's native OS confirm dialog on D is NOT a bug — it matches the documented cross-platform confirm-seam design (native plugin-dialog on desktop, window.confirm on web) already recorded in project decisions/STATE.md
decisions.rationale: Avoids mis-flagging intended platform-specific behavior as a regression just because W flagged its own web-only confirm() as inconsistent

decisions.decision: Used PowerShell Get-Clipboard to verify M6.4's clipboard-clear behavior instead of pasting into the user's real Notepad session
decisions.rationale: The Notepad window that came to foreground when launched was the user's own real session with unrelated pinned tabs (npm audit report, personal notes) — pasting a live app secret into it and leaving it there was inappropriate; PowerShell verification is equivalent and non-invasive. A fresh 'Untitled' Notepad tab was opened first but ctrl+v silently failed (0 characters) — likely a computer-use clipboard permission gap (clipboardRead/Write not requested in the original grant), not an app bug

context_notes: This is UAT Phase B (D desktop click-through) execution, ad-hoc work on feature/modern-ui-overhaul, not a GSD-tracked phase. Mid-M6, the host machine spontaneously rebooted (date rolled from 2026-09-26 evening to 2026-09-27 00:1x, ~3.5hr gap, all windows/processes gone, computer-use session had to re-establish). First relaunch attempt of pwmgr-app.exe showed a persistent blank BLACK window that never rendered content even after several seconds — had to force-kill and relaunch a second time, which then worked normally (login screen appeared). This blank-window-on-launch failure was NOT part of the formal M1.3/M1.4 script (those test a missing-asset scenario, not a cold-boot race) and wasn't logged as a UAT finding, but is worth the user's awareness as a real desktop-launch reliability issue if it recurs — consider filing it separately if it happens again. Record-only rule still applies: no fixes during UAT. Reprompt mode was deliberately reset to Per-credential at the end of M6.2 (its default/expected state for the rest of the script) — verify this stuck across the reboot before continuing.
